headline: Agents boom, offices empty, power grids strain, and a bond scare forces AI taxes

events: Spring capability jump: agentic systems reliably complete multi-day software, accounting and paralegal workflows; enterprise 'agent seats' outsell new human hires in US services
AI capex passes $900bn annualised; hyperscalers sign 20-year nuclear and gas PPAs, PJM and ERCOT capacity prices triple
US equities hit records led by a handful of AI firms while BPO hubs in the Philippines and India report first large layoffs
Fed holds at ~3.5% as electricity-driven inflation offsets disinflation in services; ECB cuts once
US-China agree a limited tariff truce extension; chip export controls remain but trade escalation stalls
Second capability jump: robotic foundation models enter warehouses, logistics and fast food at scale; customer-service employment in OECD falls ~30% in 18 months
US unemployment rises from 4.3% to 6.1% with college-graduate unemployment above non-graduate for the first time; 'graduate gap' dominates the US election
Electricity price spikes push G20 inflation to a 4.6% peak; several US states impose data-centre moratoria and grid-connection auctions
New US administration passes an emergency 'Transition Dividend' (expanded UI, wage insurance) without offsetting revenue
Philippines and Sri Lanka enter IMF programmes as services-export revenues collapse
US Treasury auction failure triggers a bond tantrum: 10-year yield hits 6.2%, Fed restarts balance-sheet purchases under 'market functioning' cover
Congress enacts a compute-and-automation levy (~3% on large AI firms' revenue) plus higher capital-gains taxes; AI stocks fall 35% then recover
Global unemployment peaks at 7.4%; large protests in Paris, Seoul, Manila and Lagos; a wave of white-collar unionisation in Europe
Japan and Korea adopt aggressive robotics-for-elderly-care programmes, turning demographic decline into an AI deployment advantage
Border clashes between Ethiopia and Eritrea escalate into open war; Ukraine front freezes into an armistice line
Pakistan and Egypt restructure debt; Kenya misses a Eurobond coupon
Productivity growth in the US hits 3.8%, the fastest since the 1950s; real GDP grows ~4% globally as AI drives down costs in software, legal, medical diagnostics
Solar-plus-storage additions surge as hyperscalers chase cheap power; renewables pass 40% of global electricity but gas and coal plants are kept online for data-centre load
EU adopts a 'Human Work Guarantee' pilot and a digital levy; trust in national governments in Europe falls to record lows anyway
Taiwan Strait naval incident triggers a three-week shipping disruption and chip-price spike, contained by back-channel talks
AI-designed drug candidates enter phase 3 trials in record numbers; first AI-discovered antibiotic approved
Unemployment eases to 6.3% globally as new care, construction, energy and AI-supervision roles absorb workers, but at lower median wages
Three firms account for over 60% of frontier model revenue; antitrust cases launched in US and EU
Policy rates settle near 3% as goods and services prices fall while energy and housing stay expensive
A Sahel-coastal West Africa conflict spills over into Benin and Togo, driven by unemployed youth recruitment
Global public debt reaches ~104% of GDP; G20 launches a compute-revenue sharing fund for debt-distressed services exporters

winners: Frontier AI labs and hyperscalers plus their shareholders
Energy and grid equipment firms, nuclear and solar developers
Ageing, high-automation economies like Japan and Korea
Skilled trades, nurses and care workers
losers: Routine white-collar workers and recent graduates
Services-export economies such as the Philippines, India's BPO hubs and Kenya
Debt-heavy governments facing higher term premia
Young workers in Africa and South Asia without a manufacturing ladder
bullets: AI agents now do most routine office work; 58% of firms use AI in production and junior professional hiring has largely vanished
Global growth averaged a strong 3.6%, but the gains went disproportionately to capital and a handful of firms, so inequality rose sharply
A 2029 US bond tantrum forced the first automation levy and set a template copied by the EU, UK and Canada
Electricity, not chips, became the binding constraint: data centres consume ~6% of global power and power bills drive political anger
Renewables reached 45% of electricity, yet fossil plants kept for AI load meant emissions only plateaued and warming hit ~1.6C
Trade tensions stayed contained; the main fragmentation is in compute, chips and data rather than tariffs
Social unrest is high and trust low; populists of left and right campaign on 'humans first' hiring quotas
Services-export developing economies suffered five sovereign debt crises as their growth model eroded
wildcard: A 2029 failed US Treasury auction triggered a global bond tantrum that directly produced the first major automation tax.
image_description: In a half-empty Manila office tower converted into a night-shift data-labelling and elder-care training centre, former call-centre workers in hard hats queue for wage-insurance kiosks while robot couriers glide past under flickering, rationed lights.
